articles.title: Civilians in Ukraine's Kherson prepare for the return of war as localized ceasefire ends
articles.description: Civilians in Ukraine's Kherson region prepare for the end of a localized ceasefire. The truce, brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump, allowed evacuations in Oleshky. It ends Sunday evening. About 2,000 civilians were in Oleshky when the truce began. They could evacuate to Ukrainian or Russian-controlled areas, or stay with replenished supplies. Meanwhile, Russian and Ukrainian drone attacks continue. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia targets Ukraine's energy systems, leaving many without power. In Kherson, the local theater continues performances, offering hope and unity.

articles.title: G20 foreign ministers end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issue, group photo cancelled
articles.description: Top diplomats from the G20 met in Atlanta, but they could not agree on important global security issues. Tensions, particularly regarding Russia's war in Ukraine, overshadowed the talks and affected the outcomes. The meeting concluded without a joint communique, only a chairman's statement summarizing their discussions. Despite the lack of consensus, efforts were made to strengthen cooperation on supply chains and mineral resources.

articles.title: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine after localized ceasefire
articles.description: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky have crossed into Ukrainian-held territory in a significant rescue operation. This happened under the most substantial truce since Russia's invasion of Ukraine over four years ago. The civilians traveled through Russia and Belarus, following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. Ukrainian authorities imposed restrictions on disclosing the number of evacuees or the border crossing location. The ceasefire in Ukraine's southern Kherson region is expected to continue through Sunday evening. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed U.S. approval of Ukraine’s purchase of 500 Patriot interceptors. Meanwhile, a Ukrainian drone attack killed two people in Russia’s Bryansk region.

The civilians traveled through Russia and Belarus, following a deal the White House says U.S. first lady Melania Trump helped to broker. Ukrainian authorities are not releasing information about how many people left Oleshky or where they crossed the border. The localized ceasefire in Ukraine's southern Kherson region is expected to continue through Sunday evening. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed U.S. approval of Ukraine’s purchase of 500 Patriot interceptors. Meanwhile, a Ukrainian drone attack killed two people in Russia’s Bryansk region.

articles.title: Civilians from war-ravaged Oleshky arrive in Belarus on their way to Ukrainian territory
articles.description: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine have arrived in Belarus as part of a major rescue operation. This operation took place under the most significant truce since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine over four years ago. Civilians began their journey out of the war-ravaged region in bus convoys on Friday. The ceasefire in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region began on Tuesday and is expected to continue through Sunday evening. The estimated 2,000 remaining residents were offered the choice of traveling to Ukrainian- or Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.
